## Security fixes

<!-- Only fill this in if you are fixing a security issue. -->

Please read [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) before opening a security PR.

Automated scanner output on its own is **not** enough to get a security change
merged. Tally Arbiter is a LAN broadcast tool: most of its HTTP surface is
intentionally open, the control plane is Socket.IO behind role checks, and
generic web-app rules produce a lot of false positives here. If you are
submitting a fix generated by a scanner or an AI agent, you must also provide:

- [ ] **A reproduction** against a running instance — the request you sent and
      the response you got back, not a rule ID or a severity table
- [ ] **The concrete impact** — what an attacker actually gains. "Information
      disclosure" needs to name the information
- [ ] **A test that runs in CI.** If the repo has no harness for the area you're
      touching, add one in this PR. Pasting a test into the description does not
      count — it has to be in the diff and it has to pass
- [ ] **Consumer check** — list what else calls the endpoint or function you
      changed (Docker `HEALTHCHECK`, the UI, listener clients, update checks)
      and confirm you didn't break it

PRs that assert verification steps that were not performed will be closed
without further review.
